text: True or False: In plural logic there is a universal plurality (some things that include absolutely everything), and correspondingly there is also a universal set of which everything is a member.
explanation: There is a universal plurality — P-Comp on φ(x) := (x = x) yields some things that include everything — but there is NO universal set (Chapter 6). The plural 'collection of everything' is unproblematic precisely because it is no object; asserting a matching universal set is the specific error, since ≺ is not ∈.
